avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducer that significantly reduces dabrafenib plasma concentrations and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if discontinuation needed, allow 2-week washout period before starting dabrafenib or after cessation

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit Juice
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor increases dabrafenib exposure and toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice; consider alternative citrus fruits

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day) with blood thinners
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate bleeding risk in patients on anticoagulant therapy, which dabrafenib patients may require
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E supplementation; monitor for bleeding signs if concurrent anticoagulants used

caution_supplements.name: Goldenseal
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 inhibition may modestly increase dabrafenib exposure
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased adverse effects; use cautiously and report symptoms to healthcare provider

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin (high doses)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May inhibit CYP3A4 at high doses, potentially increasing dabrafenib levels
caution_supplements.action: Use standard culinary amounts; discuss high-dose supplementation with oncology team

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases dabrafenib bioavailability and toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Eliminate grapefruit and grapefruit juice from diet; include in patient education

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase dabrafenib absorption rate; modest effect on overall exposure
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent meal timing and fat content; dabrafenib should be taken with or without food consistently

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, Brussels sprouts)
caution_foods.mechanism: May induce CYP1A2 and UGT at very high intakes, potentially reducing dabrafenib levels
caution_foods.action: Consume in normal dietary amounts; excessive supplemental intake should be avoided

monitoring_notes: Dabrafenib has narrow therapeutic window; monitor for loss of efficacy with enzyme inducers and increased toxicity (rash, diarrhea, photosensitivity) with enzyme inhibitors. Coordinate all supplements and dietary changes with oncology team due to critical nature of BRAF-mutant cancer treatment.
